description: The mathematical foundations of programming languages and the methods used to prove programs correct: operational and denotational semantics, lambda calculus, type systems and inference, program logics, abstract interpretation, proof assistants and effects. In the lab students step through derivations and write small interpreters, type checkers, verifiers and analysers.
modelledOn: Winskel, The Formal Semantics of Programming Languages
Nielson, Nielson and Hankin, Principles of Program Analysis
outcomes: Define the meaning of a small language by operational and denotational semantics and prove properties by induction.
Reduce lambda terms under different evaluation strategies and encode data and recursion in the lambda calculus.
State and prove type safety for a typed language, and implement type checking and type inference.
Specify and verify imperative and pointer programs with pre- and postconditions, invariants and separation logic.
Build a sound abstract interpreter and reason about its precision.
Explain how proof assistants, SMT solvers, effect systems and concurrency models support verified software.

units.title: Syntax and semantics of programming languages
topics: Concrete and abstract syntax, binding and substitution
Small-step structural operational semantics of a simple imperative language
Big-step semantics and its equivalence with small-step
Denotational semantics: domains, continuous functions and the meaning of while as a fixed point
Induction principles: structural induction and rule induction
Program equivalence and contextual equivalence

units.title: The lambda calculus
topics: Untyped lambda terms: free and bound variables, alpha equivalence, beta reduction
Evaluation strategies: call by value, call by name and normal order
Confluence and the diamond property
Church encodings of booleans, numbers and pairs; the fixed-point combinator
De Bruijn indices and writing an interpreter

units.title: Simple type systems
topics: The simply typed lambda calculus: typing rules and derivations
Progress and preservation as type safety
Strong normalisation and what it costs
Products, sums, records and subtyping
Propositions as types and proofs as programs
A first look at dependent types

units.title: Polymorphism and type inference
topics: System F and parametric polymorphism; free theorems
Let-polymorphism in ML-style languages
Unification and the principal type algorithm
Type classes and ad hoc polymorphism
Bidirectional type checking

units.title: Program logics and separation logic
topics: Pre- and postcondition triples for partial and total correctness
Weakest preconditions and verification condition generation
Loop invariants and termination measures
Soundness and relative completeness of the program logic
Separation logic: heaps, the separating conjunction and the frame rule
Verifying linked data structures with separation logic

units.title: Abstract interpretation and static analysis
topics: Lattices, monotone functions, fixed points and Galois connections
Numerical abstract domains: signs and intervals
Widening and narrowing for fast convergence
Dataflow analysis as abstract interpretation
Soundness, precision and false alarms in practical analysers

units.title: Proof assistants and verified software
topics: Interactive theorem proving: goals, tactics and proof terms
Inductive types and proofs about lists and trees
Verified software case studies: compilers, microkernels and file systems
SMT solvers and automated verification
Model checking and temporal properties

units.title: Effects and concurrency
topics: Computational effects: state, exceptions and monads
Effect systems, algebraic effects and handlers
Concurrency models: shared memory, message passing and process calculi
Data races, linearizability and memory models
Ownership types and borrow checking; session types

units.title: Research project
topics: Mechanising a type safety proof for a small language
Building a verified or well-tested interpreter
Reading and presenting a research paper in the field
Open problems: verification at scale and language design for safety

schedule.title: Syntax, binding and small-step semantics
schedule.exercise: Write the small-step rules for arithmetic expressions and assignment, derive the evaluation of x := 2 + 3 in a store, and show a proof that big-step and small-step agree on one program.

tasks.title: Write a parser and abstract syntax tree for arithmetic expressions with let-binding, and implement capture-avoiding substitution tested on five terms
Step a small imperative program through the small-step rules one transition at a time, showing the configuration of program and store after each
Implement both small-step and big-step interpreters for a while-language and test on 20 random programs that their final stores agree

schedule.title: Denotational semantics, induction and equivalence
schedule.exercise: Compute the first four approximations of the denotation of a while loop and show the least fixed point, then prove by rule induction that evaluation is deterministic.

tasks.title: Iterate the fixed-point approximations of a while loop over a small state space and show the chain of partial functions converging
Prove by structural induction that an expression optimiser preserves meaning, then test the claim with randomly generated expressions in code
Decide with a random-testing harness whether three pairs of program fragments are equivalent in all contexts, and find a distinguishing context where not

schedule.title: Lambda calculus and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Reduce (lambda x. x x)(lambda y. y) under call by value and call by name, and write addition on Church numerals.

tasks.title: Reduce five lambda terms step by step, labelling each beta step and renaming bound variables when capture would occur
Implement call-by-value, call-by-name and normal-order reducers, and run them on terms where the three strategies differ in result or termination
Encode booleans, numbers, pairs and factorial using Church encodings and the fixed-point combinator, and evaluate factorial of 5 with your reducer

schedule.title: The simply typed lambda calculus and type safety
schedule.exercise: Derive the type of lambda f. lambda x. f (f x), state the progress and preservation lemmas, and prove one case of preservation.

tasks.title: Build typing derivation trees for 5 terms, applying the variable, abstraction and application rules, and mark the term that does not type
Implement a type checker for the simply typed lambda calculus with booleans and integers, and test it on 10 well-typed and 10 ill-typed terms
Generate random typed terms, evaluate them step by step, and test progress and preservation as properties over 10000 samples, finding a planted bug

schedule.title: Richer types and propositions as types
schedule.exercise: Add pairs and sums to the typed calculus with their rules, show the proof-as-program for A and B implies B and A, and sketch the type of vectors indexed by length.

tasks.title: Match 6 logical proofs of implications to lambda terms of the corresponding types and check each with a type checker
Extend a type checker with pairs, sums and records, and add structural subtyping for records with a contravariant function rule
Define length-indexed vectors in a small dependently typed checker, type head and append, and show a program the checker rejects

schedule.title: Polymorphism and type inference
schedule.exercise: Infer the principal type of lambda f. lambda g. lambda x. f (g x) by generating constraints and solving them by unification.

tasks.title: Unify 8 pairs of type expressions step by step, showing the substitution after each step and the occurs-check failure
Implement let-polymorphic type inference with generalisation and instantiation, and test on the identity function used at two types
Implement a bidirectional checker with annotations, compare which programs need annotations against full inference, and report the trade-off

schedule.title: Hoare-style reasoning and weakest preconditions
schedule.exercise: Prove a triple for an integer-division loop with an invariant and a termination measure, and compute the weakest precondition of three assignments.

tasks.title: Build the proof tree for a triple on a three-assignment program, using assignment, sequence and consequence rules
Implement a weakest-precondition calculator for assignments, conditionals and annotated loops, and use it on 6 small programs
Find a loop invariant and variant for binary search, check them on random inputs by assertion, and spot the invariant that is too weak

schedule.title: Soundness and separation logic
schedule.exercise: State the frame rule, use it to prove a list-reversal step on two disjoint lists, and show why the ordinary conjunction fails to express disjointness.

tasks.title: Draw heap diagrams for 6 separation logic assertions and decide which heaps satisfy each, including aliased cases
Write a small heap model, check separation logic assertions about list segments, and verify a list append against its specification on random heaps
Test the soundness of a program logic against an interpreter by generating triples and executions, and find a planted unsound rule

schedule.title: Lattices, fixed points and numerical domains
schedule.exercise: Compute the interval analysis of a counting loop by Kleene iteration and show why widening is needed to terminate.

tasks.title: Run sign analysis on a small program, writing the abstract state at each point and the abstract result of each operation
Implement an interval abstract interpreter for a while-language, report variable ranges, and check them against concrete runs
Add widening and narrowing to the interval analyser, compare the iterations and precision on three loops, and explain the lost precision

schedule.title: Dataflow analysis and analyser practice
schedule.exercise: Compute reaching definitions for a small flowgraph by iteration to a fixed point, and classify five analyser warnings as true or false alarms.

tasks.title: Iterate live-variable analysis on a 7-block flowgraph until a fixed point and list the live set at each block
Implement a worklist solver for dataflow equations, run reaching definitions and available expressions, and check results on three programs
Run your analyser on 10 programs with known bugs, count true and false alarms, and tune the abstraction to reduce false alarms without missing a bug

schedule.title: Proof assistants and automated verification
schedule.exercise: Prove that appending an empty list is the identity by induction, write the proof script step by step, and sketch what a verified compiler theorem states.

tasks.title: Step through a tactic proof of commutativity of addition on natural numbers, recording the goal after each tactic
Encode verification conditions for three small functions as constraints, check them with a simple solver or enumeration, and read the counterexample for the faulty one
Model a mutual exclusion protocol as a state graph, check a safety and a liveness property by exploration, and extract the counterexample trace

schedule.title: Effects and concurrency
schedule.exercise: Model exceptions as a monad, write a handler for a state effect, and explain how a borrow checker rules out a data race.

tasks.title: Write a state monad and an exception monad in code and use them to sequence a small stateful computation with an error case
Explore all interleavings of two threads incrementing a shared counter, count the distinct final values, and mark the racy interleavings
Implement a simple ownership and borrow checker for a tiny language, and test it on 10 programs with aliasing and use-after-move errors

schedule.title: Research project in language theory
schedule.exercise: Present a research paper from the field in ten minutes: the problem, the technique, the main theorem, and one limitation.

tasks.title: Read a short paper on a type system, reproduce one of its examples in code, and summarise the claim and its evidence in five sentences
Build an interpreter for a small typed language with a type checker, and test it against an executable specification on 100 random programs
Specify a small language with its typing and evaluation rules, test progress and preservation exhaustively on small terms, and write the proof outline of the safety theorem
